A pivot is not just a pivot: Get water application right

Reinke Manufacturing celebrates its E3 pivot and the release of new irrigation innovations.

Curt Arens,senior editor of Nebraska Farmer,Nebraska FarmerOctober 8, 2026

schedule4 Min Read

A consistent coupler system from the center point to the end of the pivot offers more effective and consistent water application on the award-winning E3 pivot from Reinke Manufacturing. In addition, the company announced the release of new capabilities in its RC3 family of irrigation solutions. Curt Arens

Solving grower problems. That’s where things start with Reinke Manufacturing, a family-owned irrigation manufacturer based in Deshler, Neb., since 1954.

Reinke’s sales footprint of center-pivot and lateral-move sprinkler systems covers more than 40 countries, and this spring, the company announced key additions to its RC3 family of irrigation solutions to make life easier for its irrigator customers.

These innovations include the RC3 EOS, which delivers complete system monitoring and limited remote control through an easy-to-access interface.

Powered by ReinCloud software, it works with most pivot brands. The rollout of EOS came at the same time as RC3 Well, so producers could monitor water usage and link well controls to irrigation. This is located at the well station and offers monitoring of water pressure as it connects to other RC3 devices.

Finally, RC3 Dual consists of an EOS mounted on the last tower of the system, and an Ultimate mounted at the main control panel. This includes an RC3 expansion module, so it provides additional sensor inputs.

Related:Where has all the water gone in Nebraska’s Panhandle?

Innovation award

Then, this fall, Reinke’s Electrogator 3, or E3 pivot, was honored with an AgTech Breakthrough Irrigation Innovation of the Year Award, which is part of AgTech Breakthrough, a market intelligence and recognition platform for global technology.

“One of the things people want to say is that a pivot is a pivot,” said Chris Roth, Reinke CEO. “But it’s not. We were able to think about where the future of irrigation is and where it is going. We talk about precision all the time, but we were thinking about precision on the mechanical side with the E3.”

Using water as efficiently and effectively as possible is what consumers want from farmers, Roth said. “So, we make the E3 with consistent coupler spacing, from the center point to the end, including those with an end gun or corner system,” he explained, “because we aren’t just talking about water application, as producers are fertigating and applying chemicals too” through the pivot.

RC3 irrigation solutions were designed to be seamless with the ReinCloud telemetry platform, for ease of use by producers. Producers such as Justin Kinnan of Cozad, Neb., are excited about the ability to use ReinCloud on a mixed fleet of pivots. (Reinke)

Goals in mind

“The three areas we talk about most with growers are the efficient use of water, remote water management capabilities and helping them make good watering decisions, so they get the maximum yield for each drop they apply,” Roth said.

“Some controls were at the end of the system, some were at the pivot center, others at the well. Each had a separate interface to control point. We needed to make it where the hardware didn’t determine the user experience, but the other way around.”

Related:Save water with these drought-tolerant crops

The RC3 family of irrigation management solutions — like EOS, Well and Dual —was designed to provide seamless integration with the ReinCloud platform, so producers could manage the entire system from anywhere.

Justin Kinnan farms near Cozad, Neb., and has been using ReinCloud the past two years. “I really like the app because it is kind of self-explanatory how to use,” he said. “It is just like the touch screen Reinke has at their panels, so anyone can figure it out.”

Kinnan gets service from technicians with Holdrege Irrigation locally, and he said that the support he receives is extremely useful.

Managing a mixed fleet

“We have several Reinke pivots ranging from 2013 through 2024, and every one of them has a swing arm,” Kinnan said. “Reinke is adding the ability for ReinCloud to manage multiple brands of pivots, so you have one app for all of them. For me, that is really nice to be able to place other vendors on this same app and not have to manage three different apps.”

Many irrigators have a mixed brand fleet of systems like Kinnan does.

“RC3 and ReinCloud were designed together, rather than bolted on, so control, monitoring and decision support live in one place,” Roth added. “And because RC3 works on most electric pivot brands, a grower can standardize on one platform across a mixed fleet.”

Roth noted with that ability and the other innovations Reinke has released, “Everything we build starts with a grower problem. If it doesn’t save water, save time or protect yield, it doesn’t get much attention.”

About the Author

Curt Arens

senior editor of Nebraska Farmer, Nebraska Farmer

Curt Arens began writing about Nebraska’s farm families when he was in high school. Before joining Farm Progress first as a field editor in 2010, and then as editor of Nebraska Farmer in 2021, he had worked as a freelance farm writer for 27 years for newspapers and farm magazines, including Nebraska Farmer. His real full-time career during this period was farming his family’s fourth-generation land near Crofton, Neb., where his family raised corn, soybeans, wheat, oats, alfalfa, cattle, hogs and Christmas trees.

Curt and his wife, Donna, have four children: Lauren, Taylor, Zachary and Benjamin. They are active in their church and St. Rose School in Crofton, where Donna teaches. The family now rents out their crop ground to a neighbor, but still lives on the same farm first operated by Curt's great-grandparents. The family runs a few cows and other assorted 4-H and FFA critters.

Previously, the 1986 University of Nebraska animal science graduate wrote a weekly rural life column, developed a farm radio program and wrote books about farm life. He received media honors from the Nebraska Forest Service, Center for Rural Affairs, Nebraska Association of County Extension Boards and Nebraska Association of Natural Resources Districts.

He wrote about the spiritual side of farming in his 2008 book, Down to Earth: Celebrating a Blessed Life on the Land, garnering a Catholic Press Association award.

translationZh:
**解决问题。这就是Reinke Manufacturing的出发点。**这家位于内布拉斯加州Deshler的家族灌溉设备制造商自1954年以来一直致力于此。

Reinke的中心支轴式和横向移动式喷灌系统的销售网络覆盖40多个国家。今年春天，该公司宣布了RC3系列灌溉解决方案的重要新增功能，旨在让其灌溉客户的生活更加便捷。

这些创新包括RC3 EOS，它通过易于访问的界面提供完整的系统监控和有限的远程控制。

该产品由ReinCloud软件驱动，可与大多数品牌的喷灌机配合使用。EOS的推出与RC3 Well同步进行，使生产者能够监测用水量并将水井控制与灌溉相连接。RC3 Well安装在水井站，可监测水压，并与其他RC3设备连接。

最后，RC3 Dual由安装在系统最后一个塔架上的EOS和安装在主控制面板上的Ultimate组成。它包含一个RC3扩展模块，可提供额外的传感器输入。

**创新奖项**

今年秋天，Reinke的Electrogator 3（即E3喷灌机）荣获了AgTech Breakthrough年度灌溉创新奖。AgTech Breakthrough是一个面向全球科技的市场情报和认可平台。

“人们常说喷灌机就是喷灌机，”Reinke首席执行官Chris Roth说，“但事实并非如此。我们能够思考灌溉的未来在哪里、将走向何方。我们一直在谈论精准，但我们在E3上思考的是机械层面的精准。”

Roth表示，尽可能高效地利用水资源是消费者对农民的期望。“因此，我们在制造E3时采用了从中心点到末端一致的耦合器间距，包括配备末端喷枪或角臂系统的机型，”他解释道，“因为我们谈论的不仅仅是施水，生产者还通过喷灌机进行施肥和施药。”

RC3灌溉解决方案被设计为与ReinCloud遥测平台无缝集成，方便生产者使用。像内布拉斯加州Cozad的Justin Kinnan这样的生产者，对能够在混合品牌的喷灌机群上使用ReinCloud感到非常兴奋。

**目标明确**

“我们与种植者讨论最多的三个领域是：高效用水、远程水管理能力，以及帮助他们做出良好的灌溉决策，从而让每一滴水都能获得最大产量，”Roth说。

“有些控制设备在系统末端，有些在喷灌机中心，还有一些在水井处。每个控制点都有独立的界面。我们需要让硬件不再决定用户体验，而是反过来。”

RC3系列灌溉管理解决方案——如EOS、Well和Dual——被设计为与ReinCloud平台无缝集成，使生产者可以从任何地方管理整个系统。

Justin Kinnan在内布拉斯加州Cozad附近务农，过去两年一直在使用ReinCloud。“我真的很喜欢这个应用程序，因为它使用起来一目了然，”他说，“就像Reinke面板上的触摸屏一样，任何人都能上手。”

Kinnan从当地Holdrege Irrigation的技术人员那里获得服务，他说他得到的支持非常有用。

**管理混合机群**

“我们有几台Reinke喷灌机，从2013年到2024年的都有，每一台都有摆臂，”Kinnan说，“Reinke正在增加ReinCloud管理多个品牌喷灌机的能力，这样你就可以用一个应用程序管理所有设备。对我来说，能够把其他品牌的设备也放在同一个应用程序上，而不必管理三个不同的应用程序，这真的很好。”

许多灌溉者像Kinnan一样拥有混合品牌的系统机群。

“RC3和ReinCloud是一起设计的，而不是后期加装的，因此控制、监控和决策支持集中在一个地方，”Roth补充道，“而且由于RC3适用于大多数电动喷灌机品牌，种植者可以在混合机群中统一使用一个平台。”

Roth指出，凭借这一能力以及Reinke发布的其他创新，“我们制造的每一件产品都始于种植者的问题。如果它不能节约用水、节省时间或保护产量，就不会受到太多关注。”
contentHtml: Reinke Manufacturing celebrates its E3 pivot and the release of new irrigation innovations.
